## Welcome

Hi, I'm Thomas. I'm a PhD candidate in Statistics at the University of
Massachusetts Amherst (expected May 2027), where I work in the
[Reich Lab](https://reichlab.io) on probabilistic forecasting for infectious
disease surveillance.

My research focuses on Bayesian modeling, time series, and how we evaluate
forecasts: which scoring rules to use, and what happens when a model is fit
to the very score it will be judged by. I'm an administrator and modeler for
the [US SARS-CoV-2 Variant Nowcast Hub](https://github.com/reichlab/variant-nowcast-hub),
a collaborative platform where teams submit weekly nowcasts of variant
proportions. I'm also active in model development for the CDC's
[FluSight](https://github.com/cdcepi/FluSight-forecast-hub) forecasting hub,
where I'm a contributor to
[UMass-flusion](https://github.com/cdcepi/FluSight-forecast-hub/blob/main/model-metadata/UMass-flusion.yml),
the Reich Lab's designated ensemble submission. My WISAR6 model is one of its
components for the 2026/27 season.

Outside the lab, I've spent three summers as a data science intern in
insurance (Travelers and The Hartford), building predictive models for
pricing, retention, and loss ratios. Before graduate school at UMass, I taught
mathematics at Warren Wilson College in Asheville, NC for seven years, and I
still love teaching.

## Research interests

- Probabilistic forecasting and nowcasting
- Forecast evaluation and proper scoring rules
- Bayesian hierarchical models and computation (MCMC, generalized Bayes)
- Time series and spatio-temporal modeling
- Machine learning for predictive modeling
